chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan from Ibn Muskhan from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi said:

A man complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about poverty and debt in trade, after having had wealth in which he could meet his needs, but then his livelihood became straitened. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ordered him to go to the station of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) between the grave and the pulpit, to pray two rak'ahs, and to say one hundred times:

"O Allah, I ask You by Your power and Your ability and Your might and what Your knowledge encompasses, to facilitate for me from trade that which is most abundant in provision, most extensive in grace, and best in outcome."
The man said: I did what Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ordered me to do, and whenever I turned to any matter after that, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, provided for me.

key_terms.مَقَامَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the station of the Messenger of Allah (a specific spot in the mosque)

ai.seo_question: What supplication did Imam al-Sadiq recommend for someone suffering from debt and difficulty in trade?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the spiritual remedy for economic distress through the intercession of the Prophet’s station (Maqam Ibrahim) and the invocation of Allah’s attributes of power and knowledge. It underscores the Shia emphasis on combining practical effort with specific devotional acts, where the supplication explicitly links divine omnipotence to the facilitation of trade. The immediate success of the man’s ventures illustrates the efficacy of this prescribed ritual in restoring barakah (blessing) to one’s livelihood.
